0.0.n: This noun identifies the place whose nearest station is being discussed.

0.1.n: Links 学校 to 最寄り駅, showing which place the station is nearest to.

0.2.n: 最寄り means nearest; together with 駅, it refers to the station closest to the school.

0.3.n: Marks the destination reached with 着く.

0.4.n: Polite past form of 着く, indicating that the arrival is complete.

1.0.n: Comes directly before 日 to identify the particular day being shown.

1.1.n: この日 refers to the day shown or discussed, not necessarily today.

1.2.n: Links この日 to お昼ご飯, identifying which day's meal it is.

1.3.n: Combines with ご飯 to form お昼ご飯; お adds a polite, familiar touch.

1.4.n: Although ご飯 can mean cooked rice, here it forms part of お昼ご飯, meaning lunch.

1.5.n: Politely ends the statement identifying the meal; the subject is left unstated.

2.0.n: Places the teaching in the current period, not necessarily this exact moment.

2.1.n: て-form of 教える plus いる describes ongoing teaching and comes before レベル to specify which level.

2.2.n: A borrowed word referring here to the Japanese proficiency level being taught.

2.3.n: Marks the level currently being taught as the topic of the sentence.

2.6.n: Part of Ｎ４, the name of a Japanese-Language Proficiency Test level.

2.7.n: Links Ｎ４ to 後半, identifying the level whose latter half is being taught.

2.8.n: Refers here to the second half of the N4 material.

2.9.n: Politely ends the explanation of the current teaching level.

3.1.n: Part of the textbook title みんなの日本語, not a reference to the people using it.

3.2.n: Links みんな and 日本語 within the textbook title, literally Everyone's Japanese.

3.3.n: Names the language and forms part of the textbook title みんなの日本語.

3.5.n: Links the textbook title to ２, specifying its second volume.

3.6.n: The number identifies the second volume of the named textbook.

3.7.n: Marks the textbook volume as the thing being used.

3.8.n: て-form of 使う plus います politely describes ongoing use; the subject is unstated.

0.tip: に marks the destination with 着く, and 着きました makes the arrival polite and past.

1.tip: この日 means this particular day, so it need not mean today.

2.lit: Now teaching level, as for, N4's latter half is.
2.tip: 教えている comes before レベル to describe it: the level I am teaching.

3.tip: The の after the textbook title connects it to ２, identifying volume two.
